title: Tenant-cooperative version handshake to avoid capacity cliffs during pool transitions
creator: Ariel Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated GPU pool upgrades (runtime, drivers, or model runtime images) can produce transient capacity cliffs when many nodes are drained simultaneously. Existing soft-drain flows reduce impact but still cause tenant blips at scale due to autoscaler reaction and admission window oscillation.

Goal: Implement a tenant-cooperative version handshake that coordinates upgrade waves with tenant admission windows and the autoscaler to preserve effective capacity, minimize preemption, and keep p95 latency within SLA for hit-tenants during transitions. The handshake should: 1) reserve a small, guaranteed admission buffer per-tenant during their migration wave; 2) provide an explicit autoscaler contract to avoid rapid scale-downs while drains are in-flight; 3) expose per-tenant progress and backpressure signals to the Console and runbooks so SREs/SEs can operate with clear visibility.

Non-goals: Full multi-region live migration, rebalancing tenant workload across regions, or changes to billing/pricing models at this stage.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: scoped handshake components: Lease token service, admission-window API, autoscaler contract extension, console progress UI. Attendees: Ariel, Marco, Priya, SRE oncall.

2026-03-04 - Spike results: simulated 500-tenant synthetic load with current soft-drain: median throughput drop 6%, elevated admission rejections. Implemented naive token reservation reduced throughput drop to ~1.2% in simulation but introduced head-of-line waits for some tenants. Need fairness and reclaim rules.

2026-03-06 - Design review notes: prefer a short-lived lease token (default 10m) per-tenant per-wave. Tokens grant admission priority and a soft capacity buffer counted separately from autoscaler's observed capacity. Autoscaler contract will expose a drain-in-flight flag so autoscaler applies hold-off for scale-downs for N minutes after wave start. Action: Marco to draft API + proto, Priya to prototype autoscaler flag, SRE to author runbook stub.

2026-03-08 - Security review kickoff: tokens will be scoped and signed via control-plane KMS. No tenancy of secrets on hosts. Security flagged audit logs required for lease issuance and revocation. Marked security_review_required = true for tracking (decision later: manual attestation absent new crypto libraries).

2026-03-09 - Trade-offs discussed: aggressive reservation reduces customer-impact risk but increases gross capacity needs and costs. We decided on adaptive reservation: base reservation 2% of tenant active slots or min 1 slot, capped by tenant SLA tier. This preserves predictable unit economics while protecting high-SLA tenants.

2026-03-10 - PR feedback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128 opened by Marco. Reviewers asked for clearer invariants: (a) token issuance atomicity with drain wave state, (b) revocation semantics on failure, (c) metrics instrumentation. Marco will add integration tests and a synthetic soak job in CI to validate no regressions under network partitions.

2026-03-11 - Next steps: implement autoscaler hold-off (Priya), finish token service integration tests (Marco), create dashboard (SRE) and an alert for unexpected admission_rejections > 0.5% during a wave. Plan a small internal canary (5% of pools) after integration tests pass.
